# The boundary cases that do not hold yet.
#
# One case per line: the test's own name for it, a space, and why it is here.
# Everything not on this list must hold, and everything on it must still fail.
# CI checks both directions, which is what makes this a ledger rather than a
# list of excuses:
#
#   a case fails and is NOT here  →  a new break, on the commit that made it
#   a case holds and IS here      →  it was fixed; take it off, in that commit
#
# So the file can only shrink, and it cannot shrink quietly. That is the same
# discipline the generated reference already lives under: the gate is not that
# the number is small, it is that the number cannot move without somebody saying
# so in the same commit.
#
# Every line here is a finding from the external audit of 2026-08-24 (D45), and
# every one of them is fixed by P6-24. When this file has only comments left,
# the trust-boundary group is closed.

exec/flood-empty-frames           M-9 · frames carrying no bytes never advance the ceiling, so the loop never ends
exec/flood-unknown-stream         M-9 · the stream switch has no default; an unknown name is skipped forever
exec/flood-blank-lines            M-9 · proto.Reader.Read skips blank lines without bound, inside one call
exec/never-answers                M-9 · no host-side deadline on the exec channel; every other guest channel sets one
team/timeout-recv                 H-3 · a guest's timeout_ms has a floor and no ceiling; 1<<40 parks a goroutine for years
team/timeout-ask                  H-3 · the same number on the ask path
team/store-key-count              H-4 · nothing counts keys, and no agent can remove one
team/store-key-length             H-4 · a key is never measured against the budget its value is measured against
team/store-no-delete              H-4 · the store is append-only for the life of the team
team/refusal-keeps-payload        H-5 · a refused message's body is written to the record beside the digest
shim/sandbox-count                H-6 · nothing bounds how many sandboxes one caller may ask the shim to build
shim/no-authentication            H-6 · no route asks who is calling; documented as deliberate, recorded so it stays visible
control/guest-controls-the-terminal  found while building the OpTrust stub · a guest's refusal reaches the operator's terminal with its control bytes intact
